metadata.description: The declarative desired state of a host interface — addressing method, routes, DNS, bond, bridge and VLAN membership — as an estate record. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): NMstate is the declarative interface-configuration contract every host provider can apply, so a profile is one deliverable independent of which host realizes it. UDLM owns the identity and the version-pinned conformance pointer; NMstate owns the body (adopt by reference). Maps one to one to a Kubernetes-NMState NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy desired state.

zone.description: What kind of network this is — a governed network-zone term, for placement only (common-elements.schema.json `network_zone_ref`).

tier.description: How good this network is — a governed network_tier floor the provider reports (common-elements.schema.json `network_tier_ref`).

nmstate_schema_version.description: The NMstate interface-schema version the `desired_state` body conforms to. A new NMstate release does not force a UDLM change; the pointer moves.

desired_state.description: The NMstate desired-state body, interpreted against `nmstate_schema_version` and not restated field by field: `state`, `ipv4`/`ipv6`, the type sub-objects (`vlan`, `link-aggregation`, `bridge`, `mac-vlan`), `routes`, `dns-resolver`.

applied.description: Whether the desired state is applied and matches on the host (Realized).

discovered_state.description: The NMstate current-state read back from the host; a diff vs desired_state is drift (OBS-001).

relationships.name: configures
relationships.description: configures — the adapter/port this profile applies to. Host-side declaration (dependent-side rule).

adopts.role: the whole config body by reference (Tier-2): state/ipv4/ipv6/vlan/link-aggregation/bridge/mac-vlan/routes/dns-resolver — NetworkManager declarative desired-state, 1:1 with Kubernetes-NMState NNCP

context.purpose: Captures a host interface's desired network configuration — addressing, routes, DNS, bond/bridge/VLAN membership — as declarative state a provider applies.
context.plain_description: What a host interface's network configuration should be, in NMstate's own schema: the opaque body is `desired_state`, interpreted against the pinned `nmstate_schema_version` it declares — the profile does not re-describe NMstate's fields. A NetworkManager-family provider applies it (a configuration-management engine, Kubernetes-NMState); the state read back from the host is published, and a difference between desired and discovered is drift. It replaces per-tool host-network variable files with one governed record per interface.
use_when: You need host interface config (static addressing, routes, VLANs on a bond) declared once and converged by automation.
You need drift in host networking detected from data, not by logging into hosts.
not_for: The interface device itself — NetworkInterface; the profile configures a device that type inventories.
BIOS settings — the host's `firmware` element and, for vendor attribute sets, a Provider Class under Machine.BareMetalHost.
works_with: NetworkInterface — the adapter or port the profile applies to.
VLAN — the segments the configured VLANs and sub-interfaces ride.
